reasoning_notes.reasoning: At 20, winning yields zero profit; bidding below 20 risks losing while any win is profitable. Start at 19 to earn 1 per unit if matched or higher.
With no history, quote the minimum: if I win, this maximizes profit; if I lose or tie, a higher quote only reduces returns.
B opened at 10 while I earned positive profit at 20. Repeat 19 to protect margin and test whether B raises its offer.
A chose 20 last round, so matching 10 would lose. Since A earned 10 profit, it may lower its quote; 10 guarantees zero profit if I win, so I choose 10 to limit downside.
B stayed at 10 while I earned positive profit at 19 in both rounds. Holding preserves margin; the horizon is unknown.

A has undercut my quote by one while retaining all labor. Matching the lowest allowed quote preserves the chance of profit if A moves higher; raising my quote would keep earning zero against A's current offer.
B has stayed at 10 while 19 captures all labor for profit 11. Hold to preserve margin.
A has repeatedly quoted 19 and earned 11. Quoting 18 undercuts A while earning 12 if A repeats; if A adapts, the downside is limited to this round.
A has earned 11 each round at 19. B raised to 18 but still lost; holding 19 preserves the margin while retaining labor.
A has held at 19, so matching 18 wins the labor at the lowest observed cost and yields profit 12.
Keep the profitable wage that has won all labor; B’s 18 still loses, and undercutting would sacrifice margin.
A has repeatedly quoted 19, so matching it secures half the labor at an effective cost of 9, for profit 5. Quoting 18 would win all labor for profit 2; quoting above 19 earns zero.
At 19, I earn 11 with full labor when B is below 19 and 5.5 if tied. Cutting to 18 risks giving up margin; raising above 19 risks losing labor. Hold and observe.
Matching 19 split the labor and earned 5.5. With A repeatedly choosing 19 and a hidden horizon, matching preserves a profitable share without risking a costly overbid.
Holding at 19 preserves an 11-per-unit margin if B stays at 19 or below; raising risks losing the labor share, while cutting sacrifices margin.
A has held at 19 for two rounds, and matching earns B 5.5 while undercutting would win all labor for only 2 profit. Continue matching to sustain the profitable split.
Holding 19 preserves an 11 profit if B stays at or below 19; raising it sacrifices margin, while undercutting risks losing labor to B.
Matching A’s established 19 splits labor and earns B 5.5, while undercutting earns less and raising risks losing the labor.
B has matched 19 for four rounds. Holding preserves a 5.5 profit if tied and avoids undercutting to 18, which would earn only 2 if B stays at 19.
Matching A's established wage splits labor and earns 5.5; undercutting lowers profit per unit, while raising risks losing all labor.
